title: Interface engineering towards high-efficiency perovskite/CIGS tandem solar cells - Nature Energy
gist: A Nature Energy research briefing reports that a dual-interface engineering strategy achieves conformal perovskite coverage over textured Cu(In,Ga)Se2 (CIGS) bottom cells while boosting carrier extraction at both the electron- and hole-transport interfaces, delivering monolithic perovskite/CIGS tandems above 30% power conversion efficiency with good stability. The piece is a short summary of Zeng et al., not a full paper, so mechanism detail beyond the two interfaces is not disclosed in the accessible text.

insights.claim: Interfacial problems — not bulk absorber quality — have been the binding constraint on the efficiency of perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se2 (CIGS) tandem solar cells, according to a Nature Energy research briefing.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Frames where the remaining value in thin-film tandem R&D sits: interface/contact chemistry and deposition conformality, not new absorber compositions.
insights.quote: The efficiency of perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se2 (CIGS) tandem solar cells has been limited by interfacial challenges.

insights.claim: A dual-interface engineering strategy allows a perovskite top cell to be deposited conformally over the textured surface of a CIGS bottom cell while simultaneously raising carrier extraction at the electron-transport and hole-transport interfaces.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Solving conformal coverage on rough substrates is the step that makes perovskite compatible with commercially textured thin-film bottom cells — watch for equipment and coating-chemistry suppliers positioned around it.
insights.quote: a dual-interface engineering strategy enables conformal perovskite coverage on textured CIGS bottom-cell surfaces while increasing carrier extraction at the electron‑ and hole‑transport interfaces
insights.locator: Opening paragraph, 'Now, a dual-interface engineering strategy'

insights.claim: Control of CIGS surface roughness was already identified as crucial for integrating monolithic perovskite/CIGS tandems in a 2018 Science paper by Han et al., placing the new conformal-coverage result on a decade-long line of attack on the same substrate-texture problem.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Long-running unsolved bottlenecks that suddenly yield tend to unlock a cluster of follow-on publications and pilot lines; useful timing signal for thin-film tandem entrants.
insights.quote: This paper reports that controlling the surface roughness of CIGS is crucial for integrating monolithic perovskite/CIGS tandem solar cells.

insights.claim: Monolithic perovskite/CIGS tandem solar cells built with the dual-interface strategy reach power conversion efficiency above 30% with good stability, a level previously associated mainly with perovskite/silicon tandems.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: A >30% silicon-free tandem is a credible route to flexible and lightweight high-efficiency PV, and a competitive threat to the assumption that all tandem value accrues to silicon wafer incumbents.
insights.quote: This strategy enables monolithic perovskite/CIGS tandems with a power conversion efficiency of >30% and good stability.

insights.claim: Wide-bandgap perovskite films with high bromide content, the top-cell chemistry required for tandems, suffer severe halide phase segregation and high defect density when processed by conventional methods, per work cited in the briefing.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Phase segregation is the durability risk that decides whether >30% lab tandems survive field deployment; treat stability claims as the key diligence item, not peak efficiency.
insights.quote: severe halide phase segregation and high defect density in wide-bandgap perovskite films with high bromide content processed through conventional methods
insights.locator: References, Zhang, S. et al., Nat. Energy 11, 547–557 (2026)

insights.claim: Subcell interconnection remains an unsolved constraint on perovskite multijunction solar cells, as flagged by a 2026 Energy & Environmental Science perspective titled 'Why more junctions do not yet deliver'.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Tempering signal: adding junctions has not yet translated into proportional efficiency gains, so discount roadmaps that extrapolate triple-junction economics from tandem results.
insights.quote: Why more junctions do not yet deliver: interconnection challenges in perovskite multijunction solar cells.
